ops.title: Proposer-prompt containment: retro channel lacks structural sanitization; filename residual needs a doc line
ops.description:
Final cross-repo review 2026-07-18, fable-verified after codex's cyber content filter killed its verification mid-run (known failure mode; the F0-F2 accounting repros completed first and are filed separately as fe6651c).

CONFIRMED (medium): render_retro (meta.py:345) joins RetroVerdict.summary/evidence/next_steps into multi-line text with NO sanitize_history pass, while the failures channel one line below in Campaign.context() sanitizes every reason. numbered() prefixes only the first line, so a retro line beginning '## ' lands at line-start in the proposer prompt and can forge a harness section — the structural containment every other channel enforces is missing exactly here. Requires a misbehaving trusted retro model, hence medium. Fix: per-line sanitize_history over each field, preserving the renderer's own line structure.

REFUTED as a code defect (doc amendment only): the candidate-filename channel (driver.py describe_change -> contract.py sanitize_history) is deliberate, tested structural containment — test_history_sanitizes_a_candidate_filename_injection asserts newlines collapse to a placeholder, the payload survives glued inline on the [discard] line, and no non-harness heading can form. The security-model doc's flat 'contract history carries harness-authored text only' overstates that; one sentence naming the residual closes it.

ops.text: render_retro sanitizes summary/evidence/next_steps per line; a forged '## ' retro heading cannot start a line in the proposer prompt (test mirrors test_history_sanitizes_a_candidate_filename_injection)
research-security-model.md states the candidate-filename residual: names appear inline in history lines, structurally neutralized
